questions.prompt: Which article marker is used before a singular proper name of a person (e.g. '___ Liza ay babae')?
questions.explanation: 'Si' is the singular proper noun marker placed before a person's name (e.g. Si Liza ay babae).

questions.prompt: Which article marker is used before two or more proper names of people (e.g. '___ Simon at Tom')?
questions.explanation: 'Sina' is the plural proper noun marker used for multiple named people (e.g. Sina Simon at Tom ay mababait).

questions.prompt: Which article is used before a singular common noun or place name (e.g. 'the child')?
questions.explanation: 'Ang' is the singular article for common nouns and place names (e.g. Ang bata ay mabait).

questions.prompt: How do you form the plural of a common noun like 'bata' (child)?
questions.explanation: 'Ang mga' (pronounced 'manga') is placed before common nouns to make them plural.

questions.prompt: In inverted (natural spoken) word order without 'ay', how do you say 'The house is big'? ______
questions.explanation: Inverted word order puts the predicate first and removes 'ay': 'Malaki ang bahay.'

questions.prompt: How do Tagalog adjectives form their plural form (e.g. 'mabait' -> 'mababait')?
options: By duplicating the first syllable of the root word
questions.correct_answer: By duplicating the first syllable of the root word
questions.explanation: Adjectives duplicate the first syllable of the root: bait -> ma-ba-bait, ganda -> ma-ga-ganda.

questions.prompt: What is the plural form of the adjective 'maganda' (beautiful)? ______
questions.explanation: Root: ganda. Duplicating first syllable 'ga' yields 'magaganda'.

questions.prompt: How does 'Ako ay si John' contract when the word before 'ay' ends in a vowel?
questions.explanation: The particle 'ay' shortens to ''y' when attached to words ending in vowels: 'Ako'y si John.'
